messages:
maria: quick thought — as we prep the region cutover, can we add explicit cost tranches to the routing policy so tenants get predictable behavior and fairness across regions?

alex: +1 on predictability. what do you mean by cost tranches? a per-tenant budget class?

maria: yeah, something like bucket A/B/C where each bucket maps to allowed model variants + fallback order. cheaper buckets get more aggressive quantized models, expensive buckets use full-fp models. also: we need a fairness metric so noisy noisy tenants don't hog warm-keys in one region.

rachel: sounds sensible. tradeoff is complexity in the policy engine surface. we currently have "tier" and "region_preference" fields. adding a "cost_bucket" field expands the decision space. how do we avoid exponential rules?

maria: proposal: keep policy graph the same but add a small matcher: cost_bucket in request metadata. runtime resolves bucket -> variant whitelist, and router uses existing scoring (latency/cost/region) with a bucket-derived weight modifier. minimal new policy DSL.

alex: that keeps DSL churn low. but two concerns: 1) fairness across tenants in same bucket if a single region is underprovisioned, 2) cutover behavior when region is drained or capacity shifts.

david: for (1) we could surface a soft-fairness penalty in the runtime: per-bucket token allocation windows (like leaky bucket) plus a short-term fairness correction factor based on recent served fraction. think moving-average share correction.

maria: exactly. we should avoid strict hard caps if possible — graceful degrade. for (2) during region cutover we need deterministic fallback ordering so that cross-region hedging doesn't oscillate. suggestion: when region state changes, we temporarily pin cost_bucket->variant mapping for X seconds and route hedges using stable snapshot.

rachel: pinning helps but adds potential cold cache misses. Acceptable if short. We should add a telemetry flag to detect increased cold-kv miss rate during pin window.

alex: what telemetry do we need to decide if a bucket mapping is harming latency or cost? my list: per-bucket p95 latency, per-bucket cost_per_token, bucket gini index (fairness), cold-kv-miss-rate, and rollout_failure_rate.

maria: add rollout_failure_rate and also model-fallback-frequency (how often requests fall back to higher-cost variants). we can compute a fairness index as 1 - normalized Gini across tenants' served_fraction within a bucket.

david: implementation note for policy engine: add a tiny extension point in the resolver that accepts (request.meta.cost_bucket, region_state_snapshot) and returns an ordered list of variant candidates plus a per-variant weight multiplier. keep it pluggable so we can experiment with different fairness algorithms.

rachel: agree. but owners? who will own the resolver extension and the telemetry dashboards?

maria: i'll take the policy DSL + resolver changes (maria -> RFC PR). david take the runtime fairness control and leaky-window implementation. alex can own telemetry dashboard and test harness for cutover sim. rachel will do canary playbook updates.

alex: noted. I'll add a simulator job to run traffic mixes and compute the proposed metrics. link the sim output to a new dashboard: "cost-bucket-fairness-sim".

sre-bot: deploy note: canary window must include cross-region probes to validate pin strategy. automated rollback if p95 increases by >25% for bucket A for 10m.

maria: next steps: I'll open RFC PR describing the small DSL additive (cost_bucket) + resolver hook. david and alex will attach sim runs. rachel will draft cutover canary steps.

alex: timeline?

maria: RFC early next week, sim runs mid-week, canary doc by end of week. low-risk landing but plenty of telemetry checks.

david: one more thought — add a feature-flag gating the fairness multiplier so we can A/B it per-tenant during rollout.

maria: good call. add flag + migration plan in RFC.

rachel: ack. I'll update runbook with the p95/cost thresholds before merge.

alex: I'll start the dashboard skeleton now. ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all — saving notes to the RFC thread and pinging the owners.
